title: Multi-source BFS
summary: Start BFS from many places at once: rotting oranges and nearest-zero distances.
hints: Multi-source BFS is plain BFS where the queue starts with *all* the sources (every rotten orange, every zero) at distance 0. Push them all before the loop begins; the rings then expand from all of them simultaneously.

`minutes_to_rot`: count fresh oranges while scanning and enqueue the rotten ones. When BFS rots a neighbour, decrement the fresh count and record `minute[nr][nc] = minute[r][c] + 1` (or process the queue in whole levels). The answer is the largest minute reached, but only if the fresh count ended at 0, otherwise `-1`. Remember: no fresh oranges at all means 0 minutes.

`distance_to_nearest_zero`: initialise a result grid to `-1`; every `0` cell gets distance 0 and goes in the queue. Then BFS: any neighbour still at `-1` gets `dist + 1` and is queued. Because BFS reaches a cell first from its closest source, the first assignment is the minimum.
